codec.name: postcard
rules: enum variants are the varint (LEB128, u32) of the variant index — tables below are the pinning contract
signed ints (i16/i32/i64) are zigzag-varints (none appear in V1 payloads)
option<T> is a 0x00/0x01 tag byte followed by T when present
string and seq<T> are a varint length prefix followed by the items
structs encode fields in declaration order

conversation: client connects, sends Hello { proto_version, agent } as the FIRST frame
driver replies Welcome { proto_version, session_id, tree_seq, frame_seq, adapter } or Error { UnsupportedVersion }
any other first frame is rejected with Error { NotHandshaked }

each subsequent request is answered by exactly one response frame; pushed Event frames may be flushed between responses (M12: subscribe with the Subscribe domain; a connection that never subscribes never receives one)
Bye is answered by Bye and closes the connection
description: Binary-first CDP-style protocol: sessions -> targets (windows) -> domains; request/response + server-push events. This document is the contract for non-Rust clients (§16).

variants.name: FastForward
variants.payload: { ms: u64 varint }

variants.name: RunFor
variants.payload: { ms: u64 varint }

variants.name: SetTime
variants.payload: { ms: u64 varint }

variants.name: TreeChanged
variants.payload: the logical tree changed (the seq space TreeSnapshot/TreeDump report)

variants.name: FramePresented
variants.payload: a frame was presented { seq, hash } — the same vocabulary the trace recorder dedups on (§15.5)

variants.name: Log
variants.payload: a log record — one logs.ndjson-shape JSON line per record, streamed from the session thread's per-session tracing tap; the tap is opt-in (ServerOptions::log_tail), and a session spawned without it still rejects the kind with Error { Unsupported } (the log-tail milestone)

variants.name: Click
variants.payload: { x: f64, y: f64, button: PointerButtonV1, count: u32 varint (Playwright clickCount: 1 = click, 2 = double-click) } → GestureDone; synthesized as move→down→up ×count (§9)

variants.name: Drag
variants.payload: { from_x: f64, from_y: f64, to_x: f64, to_y: f64, button: PointerButtonV1 } → GestureDone; down→ratchet-interpolated moves (adapter pacing, ~5 px/tick)→up (§9)

variants.name: Wheel
variants.payload: { dx: f64, dy: f64 } → GestureDone; logical-px deltas

variants.name: Key
variants.payload: { key: string, modifiers: seq<string> } → GestureDone; synthesized as down→up (§8.4 key-name vocabulary)

variants.name: Type
variants.payload: { text: string } → GestureDone; one TextInput commit — adapters translate to IME or per-key events (§4.2)

variants.name: StartRecording
variants.payload: — → Codegen

variants.name: StopRecording
variants.payload: — → Codegen

variants.name: EnableOverlay
variants.payload: — → Pong; the §13 live overlay session composites hover outlines + interactive-role badges at present time (M8)

variants.name: DisableOverlay
variants.payload: — → Pong; drops the overlay + highlight

variants.name: Highlight
variants.payload: { node: option<NodeKeyV1> } → Pong; aims the hover outline (None clears it); implies EnableOverlay — Unsupported without an overlay surface (§6.2)

variants.name: InstallSeam
variants.payload: { id: string, response: option<string> }

variants.name: Clear
variants.payload: { id: string }

variants.name: ResetState
variants.payload: { scope: string }

variants.name: Call
variants.payload: { id: string, scope: string }

variants.name: Window
variants.payload: — → Shot; the full window frame, rendered once (§10 render-on-demand path)

variants.name: Element
variants.payload: { selector: SelectorV1, timeout_ms: u64 varint } → Shot; resolve the node (auto-wait Attached within timeout_ms, §8.2) and crop the window frame by the resolved physical bounds — never a re-render (§10 element rule)

variants.name: Full
variants.payload: — → TreeDump; the whole logical tree, depth-first per window root (§16 v0.4), each row carrying key/role/name/value/bounds/children — the CDP 'DOM snapshot' analog (M11)

variants.name: Filtered
variants.payload: { selector: SelectorV1, timeout_ms: u64 varint } → TreeDump; resolve the node (auto-wait Attached within timeout_ms, §8.2, honoring the connection's window scope) and dump only the depth-first walk rooted at the match (M13)

variants.name: On
variants.payload: { kinds: seq<EventKindV1> } → Subscribed; subscribe (or re-subscribe) this connection to the named event kinds — all-or-nothing: naming an unsupported kind fails the whole request with Error { Unsupported } (M12)

variants.name: Off
variants.payload: — → Subscribed { kinds: [] }; drop the connection's subscription

variants.name: Start
variants.payload: { opts: VideoOptsV1 { fps: u32 varint (0 = driver default), dir: option<string> (client-owned artifact dir) } }

variants.name: List
variants.payload: — → Windows

variants.name: Use
variants.payload: { handle: string (WindowInfoV1.handle) } → WindowUsed | Error { UnknownWindow }; aims the CALLING connection at the target — subsequent Resolves only see that window's subtree (per-connection state, §16 v0.4)

events.name: FramePresented
events.payload: { seq: u64 varint, hash: u64 varint }

requests.name: Action
requests.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, action: SemActionV1, force: bool, timeout_ms: u64 varint }

requests.name: Input
requests.payload: { events: seq<InputEventV1> } — injected into the sending connection's active window target (M7) → InputQueued

requests.name: ResolveAll
requests.payload: { selector: SelectorV1 } — the §8.2 set read (the kit's count()/all() walk, non-strict, never waits) → ResolvedAll; the connection's window scope narrows the walk exactly like Resolve (M30)

requests.name: HitTest
requests.payload: { x: f64, y: f64 } — the §8.3 hit-test read: which node occupies the point (physical px, the tree's bounds space — the dump rows' bounds, the resolve rects) → HitTest; the connection's window scope narrows the answer like the resolve paths, empty space answers None (the read is total, M32)

requests.name: Describe
requests.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint } — the §8.1 node-describe read (M36): one node's identity facts for a handle the client already holds (a resolve/hit/dump row, the dump-row rule) → Described; handle-addressed, so no window scope applies (the Action boundary), and the generation guard is the Action boundary's — a stale handle is Error { StaleGeneration }, an unknown one Error { UnknownNode }

requests.name: DescribeAll
requests.payload: { selector: SelectorV1 } — the §8.2 set read carrying facts (M39, the m37 record's standing gap): the resolve-all walk's rows plus the Described identity facts, one round trip instead of one Describe per row → DescribedAll; the connection's window scope narrows the walk exactly like ResolveAll (M30)

requests.name: DescribeAllIdentity
requests.payload: { selector: SelectorV1 } — the same walk carrying the description fact beside the identity four (M64, the m62/m63 records' reserved wire change: the M38 identity family's third assertion rides the door) → DescribedAllIdentity; the M39 encodings stay byte-pinned, the widening is its own domain reusing the DescribeAll payload

requests.name: DescribeIdentity
requests.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint } — the identity fact set at handle width (M66, the m64 record's named standing gap): the M36 Describe handle pair in, the M64 identity row out — the identity four plus the description fact, one round trip instead of the whole-set walk → DescribedIdentity; handle-addressed, the Action boundary's generation guard (StaleGeneration / UnknownNode)

responses.name: Welcome
responses.payload: { proto_version: u32 varint, session_id: string, tree_seq: u64 varint, frame_seq: u64 varint, adapter: AdapterInfoV1 }

responses.name: TreeSnapshot
responses.payload: { tree_seq: u64 varint, node_count: u64 varint }

responses.name: Resolved
responses.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, rect: option<[f64; 4]> }

responses.name: ActionDone
responses.payload: { frame_seq: u64 varint, detail: string }

responses.name: InputQueued
responses.payload: { frame_seq: u64 varint }

responses.name: ClockState
responses.payload: { virtual_time_ms: option<u64 varint>, paused: bool, steps: u64 varint }

responses.name: MockDone
responses.payload: { id: string, detail: string }

responses.name: Codegen
responses.payload: { code: string, warnings: seq<string> }

responses.name: Error
responses.payload: { code: ErrorCode (u8), message: string }

responses.name: VideoFile
responses.payload: { path: string, frames: u64 varint, dropped: u64 varint, duration_ms: u64 varint }

responses.name: Windows
responses.payload: { windows: seq<WindowInfoV1> }

responses.name: WindowUsed
responses.payload: { handle: string }

responses.name: GestureDone
responses.payload: { frame_seq: u64 varint, detail: string }

responses.name: Shot
responses.payload: { frame_seq: u64 varint, width: u32 varint, height: u32 varint, png: seq<u8> (PNG-encoded RGBA8) } — PNG rides the frame directly (already DEFLATE-compressed; the LZ4 blob stage would double-encode)

responses.name: TreeDump
responses.payload: { tree_seq: u64 varint, node_count: u64 varint, focus: option<NodeKeyV1>, nodes: seq<SnapshotNodeV1 { key: NodeKeyV1, role: string, name: option<string>, value: option<string>, bounds: option<[f64; 4]>, children: u32 varint }> } — depth-first per window root; children counts rebuild the hierarchy

responses.name: Event
responses.payload: EventV1 (see events) — a server-push event for a subscribed connection, flushed between responses (§15.6 bounded queue); connections that never subscribe never receive one

responses.name: Subscribed
responses.payload: { kinds: seq<EventKindV1> } — the subscription ack, echoing the deduplicated kinds now active on this connection (empty after Off)

responses.name: ResolvedAll
responses.payload: { matches: seq<ResolvedMatchV1 { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, rect: option<[f64; 4]> }> } — every current match, document order (the count()/all() ordering); each row is directly usable as an Action handle (the dump-row rule, M11); an empty set answers with an empty list (M30)

responses.name: HitTest
responses.payload: { hit: option<ResolvedMatchV1 { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, rect: option<[f64; 4]> }> } — the node under the point, None on empty space / outside the aimed window's subtree (the read is total, never an error); the hit row is directly usable as an Action handle (M32)

responses.name: Described
responses.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, role: string, name: option<string>, value: option<string>, bounds: option<[f64; 4]> } — the handle's identity facts (the dump row's facts, one node instead of a walk, M36); the handle echoes the request's and is directly usable as an Action handle

responses.name: DescribedAll
responses.payload: { rows: seq<DescribedV1> } — the set read carrying facts (the resolve-all walk's rows plus the Described identity facts, one round trip instead of N, M39); document order, an empty set answers with an empty list

responses.name: DescribedAllIdentity
responses.payload: { rows: seq<DescribedIdentityV1 { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, role: string, name: option<string>, value: option<string>, bounds: option<[f64; 4]>, description: option<string> }> } — the same walk's rows carrying the description fact beside the identity four (M64); document order, an empty set answers with an empty list

responses.name: DescribedIdentity
responses.payload: { node: NodeKeyV1, generation: u32 varint, role: string, name: option<string>, value: option<string>, bounds: option<[f64; 4]>, description: option<string> } — the M64 identity row at handle width (M66): the request's handle echoed, the identity four plus the description fact; stale and unknown handles ride the typed Error codes

title: Guiwright Protocol (GWP) wire schema

window_info.fields: { handle: string (stable target id: the AccessKit subtree TreeId for multi-window adapters, 'main' for single-window), title: string, focused: bool }
window_info.name: WindowInfoV1
